europe_now.title: French Government Agencies Hit by Cyberattacks
europe_now.summary: Cyberattacks have targeted multiple French government agencies. The incidents represent a significant security threat to national institutions.

europe_now.title: Swedish Military Moves to Seize Russian Estate Near Naval Base
europe_now.summary: The Swedish military is seeking to take over a Russian-owned estate situated near a naval base. The action highlights ongoing security measures regarding foreign-owned properties.

top_stories.title: Franco-German Industrial Dispute
top_stories.summary: France and Germany are currently in disagreement over the future of European industrial policy. The dispute reflects differing national priorities for the continent's economy.

top_stories.title: Spanish Government Response to Ceuta Migrant Crisis
top_stories.summary: The Spanish government has issued an apology to the people of Ceuta regarding the recent migrant crisis. Ministers within the Spanish government are also clashing over whether Madrid missed prior warnings about the situation.

top_stories.title: Polish MEP Charged with Holocaust Denial
top_stories.summary: Polish prosecutors have charged a Member of the European Parliament with Holocaust denial. The charges relate to claims that the politician made about Auschwitz being a fabrication.

top_stories.title: European Court Orders Release of Turkish Businessman
top_stories.summary: The European Court of Human Rights has ordered Turkey to release an imprisoned businessman. The directive represents a significant legal intervention by the European rights body.

top_stories.summary: Andy Burnham is tasked with shaping the United Kingdom’s social media ban. He may look to Australia and France for guidance on the approach.

top_stories.summary: Ukrainian strikes on Black Sea ports have caused grain export flows to stall. The disruption hampers grain export activities.

europe_now.title: German government issues warning after drone incident
europe_now.summary: Chancellor Merz declared that those behind a recent drone incident in Germany 'will pay the price'. The incident adds to heightened European security concerns over unauthorized drone activity near critical sites.

europe_now.title: Sweden moves to seize Russian-owned estate near naval base
europe_now.summary: Sweden's military is seeking to take control of a Russian-owned estate located near a key Swedish naval base, citing national security concerns. The action reflects growing Nordic wariness of Russian assets on sensitive territory.

top_stories.title: Poland's far-right MEP charged with Holocaust denial
top_stories.summary: Polish prosecutors have formally charged a far-right member of the European Parliament with Holocaust denial over remarks calling the Auschwitz gas chambers 'fake'. The case highlights ongoing legal and political battles over Holocaust memory in Poland and the EU.

top_stories.title: Brussels funds Spain's Ceuta response as migration tensions rise
top_stories.summary: The European Commission approved additional funding to help Spain manage a surge of migrant arrivals in Ceuta, an autonomous city on the North African coast. The move came as Madrid clashed internally over whether warnings of the influx were ignored and as Spain's government issued an apology to Ceuta residents.

top_stories.title: Grain exports disrupted by Ukrainian strikes on Black Sea ports
top_stories.summary: Grain exports from the Black Sea region have stalled following an escalation in Ukrainian attacks on Russian port infrastructure. The disruption has implications for global food supply chains that depend on shipments through the region.
